title: Fourth Moment Bound for Low Degree
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most $k$. Then, for uniform $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, $\mathbb E_x[f(x)^4]\leq 9^k\bigl(\mathbb E_x[f(x)^2]\bigr)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: The Fourier degree of $f$ is at most $k$
replaced:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most
$k$. Then its uniform fourth moment satisfies $\mathbb E_x f(x)^4\leq 9^k\bigl(\mathbb
E_x f(x)^2\bigr)^2$, where $x$ is uniform on the sign cube.
